story.en: Day 1 at ZipEats. Manager Priya shuts her laptop and stares right at you. "Finance wants a report — top 5 restaurants by delivered orders this month. 10 minutes." You open your SQL editor. Let's go.
story.ta: ZipEats-la ungaloda mudhal naal. Manager Priya laptop-a dhaaaam nu mooditu ungala naaraa paakka. "Finance-ku report venum da — this month top 5 restaurants by orders. 10 minutes-la venum." SQL editor open panreenga. Kaila sweat varuthu. Aana panic aagaadha — query simple dhaan!
story.hi: ZipEats mein pehla din. Manager Priya ne laptop band kiya aur seedha tumhari taraf dekha. "Finance ko report chahiye — is mahine top 5 restaurants by delivered orders. 10 minute mein." Tune SQL editor khola. Haath kaamp rahe hain thoda. Par query simple hai yaar — chill maar!
story.te: ZipEats lo meeru join chesina modati roju. Manager Priya laptop close chesi meeru velipottundi. "Finance ki report kavali — ee month top 5 restaurants by orders. 10 minutes lo kavali baa." Meeru SQL editor open chesaaru. Cheyyi kaduputundi. Kaani query simple ga undi ra — tension padakandi!

question.en: Find the top 5 restaurants with the most delivered orders this month. Show restaurant name and total order count. Sort highest first.
question.ta: This month-la 'delivered' status orders-la yaar yaar restaurants top-la irukanga? Top 5-a order count-oda kaanu. Most orders irundhu sort pannanum.
question.hi: Is mahine sabse zyada 'delivered' orders wale top 5 restaurants kaun hain? Restaurant ka naam aur order count dikhao. Highest pehle.
question.te: Ee month lo 'delivered' orders lo top 5 restaurants evaru? Restaurant peru mariyu order count chupinchu. Highest mundu.

title.hi: Orders table se saari rows dekho
title.te: Orders table lo anni rows chudandi

explain.en: SELECT * means give me every column — no filter, no condition. FROM orders tells SQL which table to look at. Think of this as opening a full spreadsheet before doing anything. You are just saying: show me everything.
explain.ta: SELECT * nna 'ella columns-um venum' nu arththam — filter illai, condition illai. FROM orders nna 'orders table-la irundhu edukku' nu SQL-ku solrom. Neenga spreadsheet-a full open panradhu maadiri. Adhu dhaan inga nadakkuthu — ella data-um paakrom.
explain.hi: SELECT * ka matlab hai 'saare columns chahiye' — koi filter nahi, koi condition nahi. FROM orders SQL ko bolta hai 'orders table se data lo'. Puri spreadsheet kholne jaisa hai yaar. Bas itna bol rahe ho — sab kuch dikhao.
explain.te: SELECT * ante 'anni columns kavali' ani artham — filter ledi, condition ledi. FROM orders ante SQL ki 'orders table nundi teesuko' ani cheptundi. Puri spreadsheet open chesinavatla. Meeru cheptunnadi enti ante — anni data chupinchu.

explain.en: WHERE is a row-level filter. It checks every row and keeps only those where the condition is true. Here status = 'delivered' removes all cancelled orders. Think of it as: go through every row, ask 'is this delivered?', keep it if yes, throw it if no.
explain.ta: WHERE oru row-level filter. Oru oru row-a check panni, condition true-aa irukara rows mattum vachu. Inga status = 'delivered' nnu sollinaaa, cancelled rows ellam poidum. Oru oru row paarthu 'ippa delivered-aa?' nu kekkuthu — yes nna vachu, no nna podu.
explain.hi: WHERE ek row-level filter hai. Har row ko check karta hai aur sirf woh rows rakhta hai jahan condition sach ho. Yahan status = 'delivered' ka matlab — cancelled orders sidha bahar. Sochna aise: har row pe jaake poochho 'delivered hai kya?' — haan toh rakho, nahi toh hatao.
explain.te: WHERE oka row-level filter. Prathi row ni check chesi, condition nijam unna rows ni maatrame unchutundi. Ikkade status = 'delivered' ante — cancelled orders anni pothaayi. Ila alochinchu: prathi row ki vellipoyi 'ee order delivered aa?' ani adugutundi — avunu ante unchuko, kaadu ante patteyyi.

title.en: Group by restaurant and count orders
title.hi: Restaurant ke hisaab se group aur count karo
title.te: Restaurant vari group chesi count cheyyandi

steps.sql:
SELECT restaurant_name,
       COUNT(order_id) AS total_orders
FROM orders
WHERE status = 'delivered'
GROUP BY restaurant_name;

explain.en: GROUP BY takes all rows with the same restaurant_name and collapses them into one row. COUNT(order_id) counts how many rows were in each group — that is your order count per restaurant. AS total_orders gives the column a readable name instead of the ugly COUNT(order_id).
explain.ta: GROUP BY same restaurant name-la irukara ella rows-a oru row-a collapse pannidum. COUNT(order_id) each group-la yethanai rows irukku nu count pannum — adhudhaan prathi restaurant-oda order count. AS total_orders nna antha column-ku oru nalla peyar vekkurom.
explain.hi: GROUP BY same restaurant_name wali saari rows ko ek row mein compress karta hai. COUNT(order_id) batata hai us group mein kitni rows thi — matlab har restaurant ke kitne orders the. AS total_orders column ka ek accha naam deta hai.
explain.te: GROUP BY same restaurant_name unna anni rows ni oka row ga compress chestundi. COUNT(order_id) aa group lo etni rows unnayo chuptundi — adey restaurant ki order count. AS total_orders aa column ki manchii peru pettadam.

steps.sql:
SELECT restaurant_name,
       COUNT(order_id) AS total_orders
FROM orders
WHERE status = 'delivered'
GROUP BY restaurant_name
ORDER BY total_orders DESC
LIMIT 5;

explain.en: ORDER BY total_orders DESC sorts from highest to lowest. DESC means Descending — big numbers first. Without DESC it would sort smallest first (that is ASC, Ascending). LIMIT 5 then stops after 5 rows. Priya gets her report. You survive Day 1.
explain.ta: ORDER BY total_orders DESC nna highest-irundhu lowest-ku sort pannum. DESC = Descending — periya number munnaadi. DESC illaamal potataa, small number first varum (adhu ASC, Ascending). LIMIT 5 nna 5 rows aanalae nirkka sollurom. Priya-ku report kedaichuchu. Ungaloda Day 1 safe!
explain.hi: ORDER BY total_orders DESC result ko highest se lowest sort karta hai. DESC matlab Descending — bada number pehle. DESC nahi diya toh chota number pehle aata — woh ASC hota hai. LIMIT 5 bas 5 rows ke baad ruk jaata hai. Priya ko report mil gayi. Pehla din safe ho gaya bhai!
explain.te: ORDER BY total_orders DESC result ni highest nundi lowest ki sort chestundi. DESC ante Descending — pedda number mundu. DESC lekunte chinna number mundu vasthundi — adhi ASC. LIMIT 5 ante 5 rows tarvata aagipodu. Priya ki report dorikindi. Mee modati roju successful ga avvaindi!

story.en: Week 3. You have settled in. Priya drops a new challenge: "I need a revenue rank for each restaurant, but separately per city. If two restaurants tie in revenue, they should get the same rank." She wants RANK(), not just ORDER BY. Time to level up.
story.ta: 3rd week. Neenga ipo settle aagiteengaa. Priya oru nalla challenge tharandaa: "Oru restaurant-ku revenue rank venum, aana oru city-la irukara restaurants-ku separate-aa rank venum. Rendu restaurants-ku same revenue irundhaaa same rank venum." Idhu simple ORDER BY illai — RANK() function use pannanum. Level up time!
story.hi: Teen hafta ho gaya. Ab settle ho gaye ho. Priya ne nayi challenge di: "Har restaurant ka revenue rank chahiye, but har city ke andar alag alag. Agar do restaurants ka revenue same ho toh same rank milega." Yaar yeh simple ORDER BY nahi hai — RANK() seekhna padega. Level up!
story.te: Moodu vaaram avvaindi. Meeru ipo settle ayyaru. Priya new challenge ichindi: "Prathi restaurant ki revenue rank kavali, kaani prathi city lo veru veru ga rank cheyyali. Rendu restaurants revenue same unte same rank ivvali." Idi simple ORDER BY kaadu — RANK() function naerchukovali. Level up time!

question.en: For each city, rank restaurants by their total revenue. Restaurants with the same revenue in the same city should share the same rank. Show city, restaurant name, total revenue rounded to 2 decimal places, and rank.
question.ta: Prathi city-la irukara restaurants-a total revenue-oda rank pannanum. Oru city-la same revenue irukara restaurants-ku same rank venum. City, restaurant name, total revenue (2 decimal places), rank — ella-um kaanu.
question.hi: Har city mein restaurants ko total revenue ke hisaab se rank karo. Usi city mein same revenue wale restaurants ko same rank do. City, restaurant naam, total revenue 2 decimal places mein, aur rank dikhao.
question.te: Prathi city lo restaurants ni total revenue vari rank cheyyali. Oka city lo same revenue unna restaurants ki same rank ivvali. City, restaurant peru, total revenue 2 decimal places lo, mariyu rank chupinchu.

title.en: Build revenue per restaurant per city
title.hi: City aur restaurant ke hisaab se revenue nikalo
title.te: City vari, restaurant vari revenue chudandi

steps.sql:
SELECT
  city,
  restaurant_name,
  ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS total_revenue
FROM orders
WHERE status = 'delivered'
GROUP BY city, restaurant_name
ORDER BY city, total_revenue DESC;

explain.en: SUM(amount) adds up all order amounts per group. ROUND(..., 2) rounds to 2 decimal places for clean numbers. GROUP BY city, restaurant_name means we group by both columns together — so Chennai + Murugan is one group, Chennai + Saravana is another group entirely.
explain.ta: SUM(amount) prathi group-la irukara ella amounts-a add pannidum. ROUND(..., 2) nna 2 decimal places-ku round pannum — clean numbers varum. GROUP BY city, restaurant_name nna rendu columns-a serndu group panrom — Chennai + Murugan oru group, Chennai + Saravana vera group.
explain.hi: SUM(amount) har group ke saare amounts jod deta hai. ROUND(..., 2) do decimal places tak round karta hai — clean numbers aate hain. GROUP BY city, restaurant_name matlab dono columns milake group karo — Chennai + Murugan ek group, Chennai + Saravana bilkul alag group.
explain.te: SUM(amount) prathi group lo anni amounts ni add chestundi. ROUND(..., 2) ante 2 decimal places ki round chestundi — clean numbers vasthaayi. GROUP BY city, restaurant_name ante rendu columns kalupu ga group cheyyali — Chennai + Murugan oka group, Chennai + Saravana veru group.

title.en: Apply RANK() as a window function

steps.sql:
SELECT
  city,
  restaurant_name,
  ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS total_revenue,
  RANK() OVER (
    PARTITION BY city
    ORDER BY SUM(amount) DESC
  ) AS revenue_rank
FROM orders
WHERE status = 'delivered'
GROUP BY city, restaurant_name
ORDER BY city, revenue_rank;

explain.en: RANK() OVER (...) is a window function — it calculates a rank for each row without collapsing the table like GROUP BY does. PARTITION BY city means restart the ranking for each new city. If two restaurants have the same revenue in a city, both get Rank 1 and the next rank jumps to 3 — that is how RANK() works. If you want 1,2,2,3 instead of 1,1,3, use DENSE_RANK() instead.
explain.ta: RANK() OVER (...) oru window function — GROUP BY maadiri table-a collapse pannaamal prathi row-ku rank calculate pannum. PARTITION BY city nna prathi new city-ku ranking-a restart pannum. Oru city-la rendu restaurants-ku same revenue irundhaaa rendu-ku Rank 1. Next rank 3 ku jump pannum — adhudhaan RANK()-oda style. 1,2,2,3 venum-naa DENSE_RANK() use pannanum.
explain.hi: RANK() OVER (...) ek window function hai — GROUP BY ki tarah table collapse kiye bina har row ko rank deta hai. PARTITION BY city matlab har nayi city ke liye ranking restart karo. Agar ek city mein do restaurants ka revenue same hai toh dono ko Rank 1 milta hai aur next rank 3 pe jump karta hai — yahi RANK() ka style hai. Agar 1,2,2,3 chahiye toh DENSE_RANK() use karo.
explain.te: RANK() OVER (...) oka window function — GROUP BY laga table ni compress cheyyakunda prathi row ki rank calculate chestundi. PARTITION BY city ante prathi new city ki ranking restart avutundi. Oka city lo rendu restaurants ki same revenue unte rendu ki Rank 1 vasthundi mariyu next rank 3 ki jump avutundi — adey RANK() style. 1,2,2,3 kavaalante DENSE_RANK() use cheyyandi.
